old_title: Trump to deliver midterms 'closing argument' in front of Reflecting Pool: Live
new_title: Polls open after Trump makes last-ditch appeal to midterms voters: Live updates

President Donald Trump is set to deliver his "closing argument" to midterm voters at the iconic Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, D.C. - a site dogged by the administration's botched repair job.
The monument has been largely sealed off to the public after a $14 million renovation caused the pool's "American flag blue" coat to peel. Pieces of the blue coating were seen floating in the water, while algae blooms turned the pool an unsightly green in the summer.
Trump has chosen to speak at the site for his final pitch so that he can also tout his efforts to renovate landmarks across the nation's capital, a White House official told Axios.
The president is due to hold nine telerallies in addition to the 2 p.m. speech in D.C. in a final sprint to the finish on Election Eve.
Elsewhere, in Michigan, the Senate race has been dominated by Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens' stunning endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed. Stevens has been accused of an enormous "betrayal" after she endorsed Rogers at a church service in Detroit Sunday.
Over 50 million Americans have already voted in this year's midterms, outpacing 2022's early turnout rate.
Trump's Election Eve schedule
It's Election Eve and President Donald Trump's schedule is packed with nine telerallies and an in-person speech at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
Trump is due to deliver his final pitch to voters at the iconic Washington, D.C. site at 2 p.m. ET.
The Reflecting Pool has been chosen because the president plans to address his efforts to renovate landmarks across the nation's capital, a White House official told Axios.
It has been the scene of controversy this year after a $14 million botched repair job resulted in the "American flag blue" coating to peel off the bottom of the pool. Algae blooms also turned the water green.
Trump made baseless claims of vandalism that didn't hold up in court.
The pool has been largely sealed off from the public this year.
Concern mounting for Haley Stevens after GOP endorsement
Haley Stevens gave a disastrous interview to Anderson Cooper on CNN Sunday night in which she struggled to explain her sudden decision to walk away from Abdul El-Sayed.
Her performance has sparked concern among fellow Democrats, with Michigan Rep. Debbie Dingell describing it as "one of the most painful interviews I've ever watched."
Joe Sommerlad has the details.
Crowd chants 'AOC for president!' at New York rally
The progressive Democrat brushed aside the call for her to run for the White House in two years' time in order to focus on the business at hand.
'Mr Veto': Trump maps a path to govern without Congress if Republicans lose control
The president appears to be already resigned to the prospect of Democrats seizing control on Capitol Hill this week and looking ahead to blocking their legislation whenever he can.
Here's more.
Trump melts down at another reporter at Mar-a-Lago Halloween party
In case you missed it over the weekend, he's the president once more lashing out at a journalist, this time for asking about the Iran war.
Brendan Rascius reports.
Watch: Haley Stevens posts endorsement video for Mike Rogers
Here's the Democrat's original post explaining her controversial decision...
...and here's some more Democratic reaction to her "sad, desperate attempt to be relevant" after losing her primary this summer.
Stevens gives 'trainwreck' interview to Anderson Cooper
The turncoat Democrat attempted to explain herself on CNN last night.
It did not go well.
Top story: Democrats rocked by 'despicable betrayal' on eve of midterms vote
Senior Democrats rounded on Rep. Haley Stevens Sunday after the defeated Michigan primary candidate broke with her party to endorse Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers on the eve of the midterms.
Stevens announced her endorsement in a video over the weekend, withdrawing her support for Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee and her former rival, after a falling-out over Israel.
"As you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away, and he's right," Stevens said. "And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the U.S. Senate today."
Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer reacted with fury, writing on X: "This is a despicable betrayal from Rep. Stevens. Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors."
Former House speaker Nancy Pelosi was also angry, posting on the same platform: "Haley Stevens has chosen to dangerously betray Michigan families' healthcare, freedoms and future with her horrific endorsement of Mike Rogers. Abdul El-Sayed must win - because Michigan and our country deserve better."
It did not go well for Stevens on the streets of Detroit either.
Trump, of course, absolutely loved it.
Here's more from Brendan Rascius.
Watch: Trump claims in Iowa he could have stopped Vietnam War in a week
Before Kansas, Trump was in Dubuque, Iowa, where he was introduced by House speaker Mike Johnson, who insisted "the polls are wrong" and praised the president for never sleeping.
Trump himself said the candidate he was there to promote, Ashley Hinson, used to be overweight, that The New York Times should be prosecuted for publishing poll unfavorable to him, that Barack Obama should not be disparaging the Cheesecake Factory's cheesecake and insisted inflation is under control, contrary to the evidence.
He also claimed he could have won the Vietnam War in a week (he promised to stop the Ukraine war in 24 hours back in 2024 - and secured five draft deferrals from Vietnam as a young man, citing bone spurs).
Watch: Trump talks Canada, Greenland and trans kids in Kansas
The president played many of his greatest his in the Midwest Sunday, musing on making Canada the 51st state and the possibility of renaming the Strait of Hormuz "the Trump Strait," claiming ownership of Greenland, joking about forced sex changes in America's public schools and, even more bizarrely, repeating his line about his own supporters not being able to afford a hamburger at Mar-a-Lago.
He also got down to the more serious business of attacking Republican Sen. Roger Marshall's Democratic challenger, Adam Hamilton, for which he was gushingly praised by the grateful Marshall.

The polls have opened for Tuesday's crucial midterm elections, during which voters across the country will decide whether Democrats or Republicans will control the U.S. House and Senate.
Democrats are looking to take control of Congress to rebuff President Donald Trump's agenda during the last two years of his term. They will need to flip four seats in the Senate and three seats in the House to receive a majority.
Trump's poor approval rating and Americans' concerns over the high cost of living and war in Iran have been key campaign issues for Democrats.
Many states that Trump previously won are at play in the Senate race, including Alaska, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina, Texas, Kansas and Iowa.
Meanwhile, in the House, Republicans are mostly on the defense, looking to hold on to battleground districts won by Trump in 2024.
The midterms are widely seen as a referendum on Trump's second term. The president made his last-ditch effort to appeal to voters Monday night, calling in to Fox News to urge conservatives to "pretend I'm on the ballot."
Millions will vote in new congressional districts
Millions of Americans are set to vote in new congressional districts this Election Day.
The change comes as a result of redistricting, which has changed the boundaries of about one-third of congressional districts, meaning the congressional map for 2026 looks different than the one used in 2024.
Voting machines down at most polling sites in Westchester County, suburbs north of Manhattan
Voting machines at most polling sites in the suburbs just north of Manhattan were down Tuesday morning due to an issue, officials said.
Scanners at most polling places in Westchester County, New York, began experiencing issues when polls opened at 6 a.m.
Voters are being instructed to stay in line and fill out a paper ballot, which will go into a secure box.
Republican Mike Lawler, who is up for reelection in New York's 17th Congressional District, said every scanner in the county was not working.
His Democratic challenger Cait Conley also posted about the issue, telling voters "don't be dissuaded and have your voice heard."
New York Attorney General Letitia James said her office is looking into the issue.
Midterms Senate poll tracker: Will the Democrats overturn Trump's key majority?
The Democrats' path to victory in the upper chamber of Congress is much tougher but is very much within the realms of possibility.
Paul Farrell has more.
Hillary Clinton says Trump has 'truly lost the plot'
Hillary Clinton had some choice words to share, speaking about Donald Trump during an interview Monday night with CNN's Anderson Cooper.
"He's totally unfettered and unhinged now," Clinton said, referring to how Trump was when he was first elected president in 2016.
"For him to go to the reflecting pool, one of the great failures of his efforts to redo Washington, and stand there as though it was a huge success and go on and on about all his projects, ripping up Washington, destroying the East Wing, building an arch that will interfere with air traffic control navigation in and out of Washington," Clinton said.
"You can't make this up! He is so focused on himself," Clinton exclaimed, later adding, "I mean he's truly lost the plot of being president for the American people, of winning a midterm election."
Midterms House poll tracker: The 10 races you need to know about
Here's a close look at the fight for the House of Representatives, where the Democrats seem all but certain to win back the majority, empowering them to launch investigations into the Trump administration and make the second half of the president's final term much more uncomfortable.
Live: Midterm election polls open after Trump makes final appeal to voters
'Gas prices are high because Trump started a war,' Buttigieg says
Pete Buttigieg, the former transport secretary, presidential contender and mayor of South Bend, Indiana, was on CNN last night with a very clear message to voters about how they got here.
He also had some sharp words for Vice President JD Vance.
Talarico makes appeal to MAGA: 'Let's actually fulfill some of the promise of his political project'
The Texas Senate race between Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton will be one of the most eagerly watched this evening.
Here's the former telling conservatives why they should vote for him.
Speaking up for Paxton yesterday was former NBA star Enes Kanter Freedom, who insisted the flailing state attorney general is "actually a very fun guy."
Polls open on East Coast for crucial midterm elections as 56m vote early
The polls opened in Vermont at 5am this morning and have just opened in New Jersey, Virginia, Connecticut and Kentucky too.
According to CNN, around 56 million Americans had already voted by mail before Election Day even dawned.
Early turnout has outpaced the last midterm cycle in 2022 in each of the major Senate battlegrounds, The New York Times notes.
In Texas, for instance, where James Talarico is taking on Ken Paxton, an estimated 7.7 million people have already voted, compared to 5.5 million four years ago, a 41 percent increase.
Early voting is also well up in South Carolina, North Carolina, Michigan, Iowa, Maine, Alaska, Ohio, Georgia and Kansas.
